paper.title: Effective leadership and decision-making in animal groups on the move

headline: Couzin 2005 informed leadership (zonal SPP): 2/3 locked clauses REPRO; N=100 reaches accuracy 0.9 at fraction 0.10 (P1); fraction-vs-N N=30->0.03 vs N=200->0.30 (P2); subgroup |offset| 15deg@40deg -> 85deg@150deg (P3)

verdicts.gate: P1 few leaders suffice: at N=100, mean accuracy > 0.9 with informed fraction <= 0.1
P2 leader economy: fraction to reach accuracy 0.9 is strictly smaller for N=200 than N=30
reasons: fraction to reach 0.9: N=30 -> 0.033; N=200 -> 0.300; need N=200 STRICTLY smaller than N=30 (observed: larger group needs a LARGER fraction — fixed zone radii do not scale with N, so the big group is sparser and less cohesive)

verdicts.gate: P3 averaging->commitment: heading offset from bisector <= 30deg at theta=40deg (averaged) AND >= 60deg at theta=150deg (committed)

extra.framing: genuine-agent (zonal SPP with informed minorities, disclosed)
extra.metric: group directional accuracy = cos(angle(group mean heading, informed goal)); two-subgroup test graded by heading offset from the bisector
extra.distinctness: informed-leadership fraction-vs-accuracy curve and a majority-vs-averaging heading transition from CONTINUOUS spatial motion — NOT the milling/hysteresis phase portrait of couzin_zonal, and NOT discrete spin/vote flips like galam_majority / majority_vote
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + lock-first discipline reproduce the informed-leadership phenomena (a small informed minority steers the group; averaging vs commitment when leaders disagree) and would catch an artifact — an honest MISS on a mis-calibrated locked bar is a valid outcome, not tuned away

citations: Couzin, I.D., Krause, J., Franks, N.R. & Levin, S.A. (2005). Effective leadership and decision-making in animal groups on the move. Nature 433:513-516. doi:10.1038/nature03236.

Couzin, I.D., Krause, J., James, R., Ruxton, G.D. & Franks, N.R. (2002). Collective memory and spatial sorting in animal groups. Journal of Theoretical Biology 218(1):1-11. doi:10.1006/jtbi.2002.3065.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the Couzin 2005 informed-leadership claims (leader economy + averaging/commitment transition)
